desc:
A network of n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1 starts without any links. The links edges[0], edges[1], ... are then added one at a time in this order, where edges[i] = [a, b] joins a and b. The same pair may be added more than once.

The network is bipartite while its nodes can be coloured with two colours so that every link joins different colours. Return the smallest index i such that the network made of edges[0..i] is no longer bipartite, or -1 if it stays bipartite after all links were added.

n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[3,4],[2,3],[4,0],[0,2]]  ->  4
(after index 4 the links 0-1-2-3-4-0 form a cycle of 5 nodes)

n = 3, edges = [[0,1],[1,2]]                           ->  -1
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < n and a ≠ b
The same pair of nodes may appear several times
hints: Checking every prefix from scratch with a fresh BFS is too slow when there are thousands of links. What information do you need to keep between steps?
A new link [a, b] breaks bipartiteness exactly when a and b are already connected and are forced to have the same colour.

Use union-find where every node also stores its colour parity relative to its parent. When joining two different groups, set the parity so that a and b end up different. When a and b are in the same group and have the same parity, this link is the answer.
editorial: Adding a link between two nodes that lie in different pieces never creates a problem: you can flip all colours of one piece if needed. Only a link inside one piece can hurt. Inside a piece the colours are fully determined up to a global flip, so the link [a, b] is fine if the colours of a and b already differ, and creates an odd cycle if they are equal.

Keep a union-find forest in which every node stores par[x], the colour difference (0 or 1) between x and its parent. The function find(x) returns the root and the difference between x and the root, compressing the path while it adds up the differences by XOR. For a link [a, b], let (ra, pa) = find(a) and (rb, pb) = find(b). If ra equals rb and pa equals pb, return the index. If ra differs from rb, attach one root below the other with difference pa ^ pb ^ 1, so that a and b get different colours. Repeating a pair that was already added is harmless.

Every link costs one or two find operations, which are almost constant with path compression and union by size. The total time is about O(m alpha(n)). Without union-find you could binary search on the prefix length and run a BFS check each time, for O(m (n + m) log m) which is much slower.
